title: Kingdom of Germany
capsule: The Kingdom of Germany (Regnum Teutonicum) crystallized from East Francia when the Carolingian line died out with Louis the Child in 911 and the dukes elected Conrad of Franconia as king, decisively breaking from Carolingian dynastic succession. Power shifted in 919 to the Saxon Henry the Fowler, who unified the stem duchies (Saxony, Franconia, Bavaria, Swabia, Lotharingia), halted Magyar incursions at the Battle of Riade in 933, and built a network of fortified towns. His son Otto I defeated the Magyars decisively at the Battle of Lechfeld in 955 and was crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope John XII in Rome on 2 February 962, at which point the kingdom became the dominant component of the new imperial framework. The title rex teutonicorum emerged around 1000 as the realm's German-speaking identity solidified, though kings increasingly preferred rex Romanorum to stress their imperial pretensions.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core stem duchies are well attested in Ottonian diplomas and chronicles; marcher frontiers with Slavic polities and the exact extent of Lotharingia's incorporation varied and are imprecisely bounded.
